sections.h2: What do Clay County's size and population mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Clay County has 604.61 land square miles and an estimated 239,593 people in mid-2025. That is 9.8% above the 218,249 counted at the start of 2020.

Households earn a median $87,820 for 2020 to 2024, more than the medians reported for Charlotte County and Citrus County, and the typical owned home is worth $312,500. Owners occupy 75.9% of 94,791 housing units, and rent runs about $1,551. Households average 2.69 people; 22.5% of residents are children and 18.8% are seniors.

The mean commute is 31.3 minutes, and 61.7% of adults work or seek work. The county also counts 27,517 veterans.

sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who values the property in Clay County?
sections.html:
Two elected offices split the job: the tax collector sends and collects the bill, and the property appraiser sets value and rules on exemptions.

Bills go out by November 1, and a homeowner whose lender pays the tax gets an information-only copy. Taxes are assessed as of January 1 but are normally payable November 1. The page cites Florida Statute 197.122 for the rule that an owner must find out what is due and pay on time, whether or not a bill arrived.

  • Property appraiser: value, homestead, portability and other exemptions, filed by March 1.
  • Tax collector: payment, installment and partial payment plans, certificate sales.
  • Clerk: records the deed and collects stamp tax.

sections.h2: What are the Clay County discounts and due dates?
sections.html:
The discount is 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February, with no discount in March and delinquency on April 1.

Every payment method is accepted. A card payment adds a 2.50% fee, while an online e-check adds none.

sections.h2: How do Clay County installment and partial payment plans work?
sections.html:
To use installments you apply by April 30 with estimated taxes above $100, then pay the first quarter by June 30.

The first installment carries a 6% discount, with no discount if paid in July, and failing to make it by July 31 cancels the plan. The second, due September 30, carries 4.5%. The third, due December 31, carries 3%, and the fourth, due March 31, carries none. The first two installments are based on the prior year's tax notice, while the last two reflect changes in ownership, value or exemptions.

Partial payments are a separate option under Florida Statute 197.374. The owner submits a Partial Payment Plan application with the first payment or in person, and payments can begin November 1. Online payment is not accepted for this plan. Early payment discounts are forfeited, so the full March amount is due, and any balance left on April 1 is delinquent and goes into the June certificate sale.

sections.h2: What happens when Clay County taxes are not paid?
sections.html:
Expect a 3% penalty on April 1, more fees from May 1, and a certificate sale by June 1.

Florida law then lets the certificate holder apply for a tax deed after two years have passed since April 1 of the year of issuance, with an application fee of $75. The clerk holds the public auction, and the winning bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater. An owner can pay the taxes before the deed issues and stop the sale.

If no one bids, the land goes on the list of lands available for taxes. Fees grow as the process advances, so request a payoff from the tax collector before listing a home with unpaid tax.

sections.h2: What does Clay County's economy look like in the Census data?
sections.html:
The Census counts 4,455 employer establishments and 48,303 paid employees in 2023, with an annual payroll of $2,210,794 thousand and employment up 5.1% from 2022. Medical and social assistance receipts reached $1,626,540 thousand in 2022 and retail sales $2,931,043 thousand.

Among 4,168 employer firms, 354 are veteran-owned. Bachelor's degrees are held by 28.3% of adults 25 and over, 94.6% of households have broadband and 9.1% of people live in poverty.

Why this matters for a seller: a county with growing employment and 1,522 building permits in 2025 sees steady assessment activity, so check your TRIM notice each August. A value petition filed with the clerk is due 25 days after the TRIM notice, and exemption denials carry a 30 day window.

sections.h2: Which Clay County deadlines trip up sellers?
sections.html:
Three dates matter most when a house is on the market. March 1 is the exemption filing deadline for any buyer who wants homestead in the first year. March 31 is the final due date for a full bill or the fourth installment, and April 1 starts the penalty clock.

The installment plan also has a July trap. A first payment that misses June 30 but lands before July 31 earns no discount, and missing July 31 cancels the plan and returns the owner to the regular due dates and discounts. If you close in summer, find out which installments are paid so the contract divides the rest fairly.

  • Application for installments: April 30.
  • Credit card fee: 2.50%, none for online e-check.
  • Partial payment: current year only, November 1 through March 31.

sections.h2: How do homestead and Save Our Homes cap work in Clay County?
sections.html:
Form DR-501 goes to the appraiser's office, and it must be in by March 1, with the home your permanent residence as of January 1.

The exemption is up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 covering all taxes and the added $25,000 covering only non-school taxes on value over $50,000. From the second year, assessed value can rise by only the smaller of 3 percent or inflation; the published chart shows caps of 2.9 percent for 2025 and 2.7 percent for 2026. Portability allows a move to a new Florida homestead within three years, with Form DR-501T filed alongside.

Non-homestead property has a separate 10 percent annual limit on assessed value growth. That matters for a rental or second home in Clay County, because its value for tax purposes can still climb every year.

sections.h2: How is the tax settled when you sell a Clay County home?
sections.html:
The closing agent prorates the year's tax, pays any amount due from your proceeds and records the deed with the clerk, so that stamp tax is collected.

A deed carries a stamp tax of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration everywhere except Miami-Dade, and the state revenue agency says all parties to the document are liable no matter who agrees to pay. Confirm which tax year your payoff covers, because partial payment rules apply to the current year only.

If a lender escrows your tax, ask for a timeline on any escrow refund, and ask the tax collector whether the current bill is already paid.

faqs.q: What are the Clay County property tax discounts?
faqs.a: They are 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February. March has no discount, and April 1 is delinquency with a 3% penalty.

faqs.q: When is the Clay County installment application due?
faqs.a: By April 30. Estimated taxes must be above $100, and the first payment is due June 30 for the 6% discount.

faqs.q: Does Clay County charge a fee to pay by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax collector's page states a 2.50% fee on credit card payments, and online e-check payments carry no fee.

faqs.q: When is the Clay County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: On or before June 1, covering the prior year's delinquent real estate taxes. Additional fees apply as of May 1.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for homestead in Clay County?
faqs.a: Apply with the Clay County Property Appraiser by March 1 using Form DR-501. The appraiser decides eligibility, and the tax collector only bills.
